tier_reason: README benchmark table comes from the public criterion harness rust/benches/glob_comparison.rs (plus rust/benches/walk_comparison.rs, driven by scripts/run-benchmarks.sh), with toolchain and flags stated (zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast static build, cargo bench) and CPU named (Intel Core i7-14700K); baseline is the Rust glob crate and globset+walkdir, both opened and confirmed in the harness source.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Linux kernel checkout, median wall time: **/*.c (36,685 matches) 24.2 ms vs glob crate 49.2 ms (2.0x) and globset+walkdir 43.8 ms (1.8x); drivers/**/*.c 8.23 ms vs 16.4 ms (2.0x); fs/*.c 9.84 us vs 31.9 us (3.2x); */Makefile 11.4 us vs 39.1 us (3.4x). Walk (185,737 entries, warm cache, best of 5): plain walk 27.4 ms vs walkdir 90.9 ms; gitignore walk 2.4 ms vs ignore 8.0 ms; parallel 0.64 ms vs 4.9 ms; walk+metadata 24.3 ms vs 226 ms. README also claims 1.2-1.7x (up to 10x) over glibc glob(), with no table.
corrections.caveats: The published tables compare against Rust crates (glob, globset+walkdir, walkdir, ignore), not glibc glob(); the glibc speedup claim has no published table or harness output on the page. rustc version is not stated (zig 0.16.0 is). Large globset+walkdir ratios (up to ~4,100x) reflect globset having to walk the whole tree for shallow patterns. README links LICENSE.md, which 404s; the license file is LICENSE (MIT per GitHub).

notes: Harness files exist (glob_comparison.rs, walk_comparison.rs, run-benchmarks.sh all fetched). Off the C++-std baseline: incumbent is the Rust glob crate; glibc claim unverified.

tier_reason: Numbers are from the peer-reviewed ASPLOS'23 paper (abstract quoted in the README) comparing GPU self-orchestrated storage access against CPU-orchestrated storage access; the repo is the artifact (asplosaoe/ directory) but compiler flags and CPU model are not stated on the page, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (ASPLOS'23 abstract): 1.0x (BFS) and 1.49x (CC) end-to-end speedup for graph analytics while reducing hardware cost by up to 21.7x; 5.3x speedup on data-analytics workloads on the same hardware.
corrections.caveats: The baseline in the paper is a CPU-orchestrated GPU storage path, not literally POSIX read/write, mmap or io_uring; README quotes the ASPLOS'23 abstract without benchmark setup. The BFS result is 1.0x (parity), with the win being hardware cost. Needs a Volta-or-newer datacenter NVIDIA GPU, a custom kernel module and IOMMU disabled; CUDA 12.3+, GCC 5.4+.

notes: Paper itself not opened (ACM blocked); tier B rests on the peer-reviewed venue and README-quoted abstract. Last commit 2025-11-23 (merge of PR #64), so active.
